question: When I export a Data Exchange revision to S3, which encryption can I apply to the exported files?
visibleText:
When you export a revision from AWS Data Exchange to S3, you set the server-side encryption configuration in the export job details. You can choose server-side encryption with Amazon S3-Managed Keys (SSE-S3) or server-side encryption with KMS keys stored in AWS Key Management Service (SSE-KMS).

1. SSE-S3: server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys
2. SSE-KMS: server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys

The Data Exchange documentation lists only these two options for exports. It doesn't mention DSSE-KMS or SSE-C as choices in the export job. If you're setting up an auto-export as a subscriber, you pick the encryption options in the console when you add the bucket destination.

Also note that all S3 buckets have SSE-S3 as the default encryption configuration, so exported objects are encrypted at rest even if you don't pick anything special. If you do use SSE-KMS, the KMS key must be in the same Region as the bucket, and there are additional charges for using AWS KMS keys.
